title: Kinetic Particle Theory
topic: Particle Model and States of Matter
subject: Combined Chemistry

questions.question: Which statement best describes the arrangement of particles in a solid?
options: Particles are far apart and move randomly
Particles are closely packed in a regular arrangement and vibrate about fixed positions
Particles are close together but can slide past each other
Particles move freely at high speeds in all directions
questions.explanation: In solids, particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces of attraction. They vibrate about these positions but cannot move freely. The arrangement is regular.

questions.question: Why does diffusion occur faster in gases than in liquids?
options: Gas particles are larger than liquid particles
Liquid particles have stronger electrostatic forces than gas particles
Gas particles are attracted to each other more strongly
Gas particles have more energy and move faster with more space between them
questions.explanation: Gas particles have higher kinetic energy, move faster, and have more space between them, allowing them to spread out and mix more quickly than liquid particles.

questions.question: A gas is compressed into a smaller volume at constant temperature. What happens to the pressure and why?
options: Pressure increases because frequency of collision of particles on inner surface increases
Pressure decreases because particles move slower
Pressure stays the same because temperature is constant
Pressure decreases because particles are closer together
questions.explanation: Pressure is caused by the frequency of collision of particles on the inner surface of the container. When volume decreases, particles collide more frequently, increasing pressure.

questions.question: What happens to the movement of particles when a substance is heated?
options: Particles move slower and closer together
Particles gain kinetic energy and move faster
Particles lose energy and stop moving
Particles become larger in size
questions.explanation: Heating transfers energy to particles, increasing their kinetic energy. This causes them to move faster and, in gases and liquids, spread further apart.

questions.question: Which observation provides evidence for the kinetic particle theory?
options: Ice floats on water
Metals conduct electricity
Bromine vapour spreads to fill a gas jar
Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level
questions.explanation: The spreading of bromine vapour (diffusion) demonstrates that gas particles are in constant random motion, supporting the kinetic particle theory.

questions.question: Why does a balloon expand when heated?
options: The rubber becomes softer when warm
Air particles from outside enter the balloon
The mass of gas particles increases with temperature
Gas particles inside gain energy, move faster, and collide more forcefully with the balloon walls
questions.explanation: Heating increases the kinetic energy of gas particles inside the balloon. They move faster and collide more forcefully with the walls, causing the balloon to expand.

questions.question: In which state of matter do particles have the most freedom of movement?
options: Solid
Liquid
Gas
All states have equal freedom
questions.explanation: Gas particles have weak forces of attraction between them and move freely at high speeds in all directions, giving them the most freedom of movement.

questions.question: A perfume is sprayed in one corner of a room. After a few minutes, it can be smelled across the room. This is an example of:
options: Diffusion
Evaporation
Condensation
Sublimation
questions.explanation: Diffusion is the spreading of particles from an area of high concentration to low concentration due to their random motion. Perfume particles spread through the air by diffusion.

questions.question: What happens to the volume of a fixed mass of gas when its temperature increases at constant pressure?
options: Volume decreases
Volume stays the same
Volume increases
Volume first increases then decreases
questions.explanation: At constant pressure, heating a gas increases particle kinetic energy. Particles move faster and push the container walls outward, increasing volume.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect the rate of diffusion of a gas?
options: Temperature
Mass of gas particles
Concentration gradient
Colour of the gas
questions.explanation: Diffusion rate depends on temperature (higher = faster), particle mass (lighter = faster), and concentration gradient. Colour is a visual property and does not affect particle motion.

questions.question: Why can gases be compressed easily but solids cannot?
options: There is more empty space between gas particles than between solid particles
Gas particles are smaller than solid particles
Solid particles repel each other strongly
Gas particles have no mass
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart with large empty spaces between them, allowing them to be pushed closer together. Solid particles are already closely packed with minimal space.

questions.question: When a liquid evaporates, what happens to the particles that escape into the gas phase?
options: They are the slowest-moving particles in the liquid
They are the particles with the highest kinetic energy
They lose energy as they escape
They change into different particles
questions.explanation: Only particles with sufficient kinetic energy can overcome the attractive forces holding them in the liquid. These high-energy particles escape as gas, leaving lower-energy particles behind.

questions.question: A sealed syringe contains air. When the plunger is pushed in, the pressure increases. Why?
options: Air particles collide with the walls more frequently in the smaller volume
Air particles become smaller
Air particles move slower in a smaller space
The number of air particles increases
questions.explanation: Reducing volume forces the same number of particles into a smaller space. They hit the container walls more often per second, increasing pressure.

questions.question: Which statement explains why solids have a fixed shape?
options: Solid particles are in constant random motion
Solid particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces of attraction
Solid particles can slide past each other easily
Solid particles have no kinetic energy
questions.explanation: Strong electrostatic forces hold solid particles in a fixed, regular arrangement. They can only vibrate about these positions, giving solids a definite shape.

questions.question: Why is gaseous fuel less preferred than liquid fuel for storage in vehicle tanks?
options: Gases are more expensive to produce than liquids
Gases burn less efficiently than liquids
Gases occupy a much larger volume than liquids for the same mass, making storage difficult
Gases are heavier than liquids
questions.explanation: Gas particles are far apart. For the same mass of fuel, the gaseous state occupies a much larger volume than the liquid state, requiring larger and heavier tanks for storage.
